en.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil Hits $400 Million, Tops Franchise Box Office
en.summary: Director Zach Cregger's take on the iconic zombie game franchise has achieved a massive global box office milestone. The film has now surpassed all previous installments in the 24-year-old series.
en.body:
It’s official: **Zach Cregger**’s bold reimagining of the **Resident Evil** universe has clawed its way to a staggering $400 million at the global box office. This impressive sum makes it the highest-grossing installment in the venerable 24-year-old franchise, a testament to Cregger's unique vision and the enduring appeal of the iconic survival horror series.

The film has amassed $157.399 million in North America, with an additional $242.6 million pouring in from international markets. This worldwide haul of exactly $400 million significantly outpaces previous entries, which often struggled to break the $100 million mark globally. The film's debut weekend alone was a franchise record-breaker, igniting excitement and proving that audiences were ready for a new take on Raccoon City's horrors.

## A New Era for Resident Evil

Cregger, known for his distinctive directorial style and sharp storytelling, has injected a fresh energy into the **Resident Evil** IP. While specific details about the film's production budget and marketing costs are not publicly available, its global performance suggests a highly profitable venture for the studio. The film’s success is particularly noteworthy given the challenges of adapting video game properties, a notoriously difficult genre to translate to the big screen. Cregger’s approach appears to have resonated deeply, capturing both the essence of the original games and appealing to a broader audience.

The film's narrative and directorial choices have clearly struck a chord with long-time fans and newcomers alike, driving repeat viewings and strong word-of-mouth. This financial triumph not only solidifies **Resident Evil**'s place in cinematic history but also sets a high bar for future installments.

## What This Means for the Franchise

This box office milestone is more than just a number; it's a powerful signal to Hollywood that audiences are hungry for well-crafted, character-driven adaptations of their favorite games. For fans, it means the **Resident Evil** cinematic universe is not only alive and well but poised for future expansion. The critical and commercial success of Cregger's film opens the door for deeper dives into the lore, more terrifying encounters, and potentially new character explorations. It validates the creative risks taken and suggests a bright future for the franchise on screen, promising more thrills and scares for years to come.

## What's Next

With **Resident Evil** now firmly established as the franchise's highest earner, anticipation is already building for what comes next. While official announcements regarding sequels or spin-offs have not yet been made, the financial success strongly suggests that further adventures in this universe are inevitable. Fans will be eagerly awaiting news on potential director attachments, cast returns, and release windows.
